tone: Use clear, concise, neutral Thai suitable for a desktop utility; avoid unnecessary pronouns and polite particles.
capitalization: Do not imitate English capitalization; preserve capitalization only inside protected Latin terms.
button_labels: Use short familiar Thai action verbs without sentence-ending punctuation.
ui_roles: Keep labels compact, buttons action-led, tooltips explanatory, and warnings or errors as natural complete messages.
technical_terms: Use established Thai software terminology and preserve protected products, APIs, abbreviations, and identifiers verbatim.
contextual_terminology: Choose ambiguous terms from the feature, stable ID, surface type, and neighboring strings; do not transliterate English automatically.
punctuation: Use natural Thai spacing and punctuation while preserving syntax tokens, placeholders, and accelerators.
units: Keep values and unit meaning unchanged and use conventional Thai spacing around Latin units.
natural_language: Use idiomatic Thai clause order and avoid word-for-word English structure.
